questions.question: When loading corrosive materials, you should not:
questions.explanation: Keep corrosive material containers in their upright position. Do not drop or roll them.

questions.question: What must the shipper include in emergency response information?

options.text: Any risks of fire or explosion.
How many people should respond in case of an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any risks of fire or explosion.
questions.explanation: Emergency response information must include the material's basic description and technical name, health hazards, fire or explosion risks, accident precautions, fire handling methods, spill handling methods, and first aid steps.

questions.question: When do you need a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement?

options.text: In a vehicle requiring a Class A license.
In a vehicle requiring a Class B license.
In a vehicle requiring a Class C license.

questions.explanation: You must have a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement to transport hazardous materials in any vehicle, regardless of size.

questions.question: Where should hazardous materials shipping papers NOT be kept?

options.text: In a pouch on the driver's side door.
In a pouch on the passenger's side door.
Within reach of the driver while wearing a seat belt.
On the driver's seat while the driver is outside the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a pouch on the passenger's side door.
questions.explanation: Shipping papers must be on the driver's side door or within the driver's reach while driving. If you leave the vehicle, place papers on the driver's seat.

questions.question: What should you do if you suspect a leak in radioactive material cargo?

options.text: Go to the local fire department.
Pick up any loose pieces of radioactive material.
Continue driving as long as you avoid touching the affected areas.
Do not drive the vehicle until it has been cleaned.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive the vehicle until it has been cleaned.
questions.explanation: If you suspect a leak in radioactive material, tell your dispatcher or supervisor right away. Do not touch or inhale the material. Do not drive the vehicle until it has been cleaned or checked with a survey meter.

questions.question: Who identifies the hazard class of a hazardous material?
questions.explanation: The shipper is responsible for identifying the hazard class, product number, proper shipping name, and packing group. The shipper also determines the correct packaging, labels, markings, and placards.

questions.question: What does a driver need to accept a hazardous materials package?
questions.explanation: The shipper certifies that hazardous materials are properly packaged. Unless a package looks unsafe, you can accept the shipper's certification that it meets hazardous materials regulations.

questions.question: After delivering compressed gas, turn off the engine ____ you unhook the hoses.
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine before unhooking the hoses when delivering compressed gas. If your engine runs a pump, turn it off after the delivery but before disconnecting the hoses.

questions.question: What must a box containing liquid containers display?

options.text: Arrows pointing in the correct upright direction.
The number of containers inside the box.

questions.correctAnswerText: Arrows pointing in the correct upright direction.
questions.explanation: Boxes with liquid containers must have orientation markings with arrows showing which direction is up.

questions.question: Which agency helps coordinate emergency response to chemical hazards?

options.text: The United Center for Chemical Assistance.

questions.explanation: The National Response Center helps police and firefighters coordinate emergency response to chemical hazards.

questions.question: What is a sign that a shipment may contain hazardous materials?

options.text: The shipper is a business that typically handles hazardous materials.
The last shipment you picked up was labeled as hazardous.
The road is made of gravel.

questions.correctAnswerText: The shipper is a business that typically handles hazardous materials.
questions.explanation: One sign that a shipment may contain hazardous materials is if the shipper is a business that typically deals with hazardous materials. Examples include paint stores, chemical suppliers, science suppliers, pest control companies, farm suppliers, and explosives or fireworks dealers.

questions.question: What does a hazardous materials shipping paper describe?

options.text: How the materials will be transported
Who should accept the materials being transported

questions.explanation: A shipping paper describes the hazardous materials being transported. Shipping orders, bills of lading, and manifests are all types of shipping papers.

questions.question: What does "RQ" stand for?
questions.explanation: On shipping papers, "RQ" may be used instead of an "X" in the hazardous materials column to show that the material has a reportable quantity.

questions.question: What shape is a hazardous materials placard?
questions.explanation: Vehicles carrying hazardous materials must display diamond-shaped warning signs on all four sides. These signs are called placards.

questions.question: Hazardous materials containers must be:

options.text: Secured to prevent movement during transportation.
A maximum of four feet tall.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secured to prevent movement during transportation.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials containers must be secured so they will not fall, slide, or bounce during transportation.

questions.question: When refueling a vehicle that contains hazardous materials:

options.text: The engine should be left on.
The engine should be turned off.
The gas nozzle may be left unattended.
No other vehicles should be at the refueling station.

questions.correctAnswerText: The engine should be turned off.
questions.explanation: When refueling a vehicle carrying hazardous materials, turn off the engine first. Someone must always stay at the nozzle and control the fuel flow during refueling.

questions.question: How many hazardous materials classes exist?
questions.explanation: There are nine hazardous materials classes. Each class represents the type of risk that a material poses.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT considered a hazardous material?
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials are products that pose risks to health, safety, and property during transportation. Hazardous materials include explosives, flammable and poisonous gases, and flammable and other dangerous solids. Rocks are not hazardous materials.

questions.question: How long must shippers keep a copy of shipping papers?
questions.explanation: Shippers must keep a copy or electronic image of hazardous materials shipping papers for at least two years after the materials are accepted by the first carrier. For hazardous waste, this increases to three years.

questions.question: Class 1, Class 2.1, and Class 3 items should NOT be transported in a trailer with:
questions.explanation: Cargo heaters are generally not permitted when transporting Class 1 (Explosives), Class 2.1 (Flammable Gas), or Class 3 (Flammable Liquids) materials.

questions.question: When transporting chlorine, what must you do at a railroad crossing?

options.text: You must stop before crossing the tracks.
You must slow down before crossing the tracks.
You can cross without stopping if no warning lights are flashing.
You can cross without stopping if no other vehicles are nearby.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop before crossing the tracks.
questions.explanation: When transporting chlorine, you must always stop at a railroad crossing. Stop 15 to 50 feet from the nearest track.

questions.question: How should placards be positioned on a vehicle?

options.text: In any way, as long as they are visible.
So words and numbers can be read from left to right.
Within three inches of other markings.

questions.correctAnswerText: So words and numbers can be read from left to right.
questions.explanation: Hazard placards must be positioned so all words and numbers read from left to right. They must be at least three inches away from other markings.

questions.question: Where should the identification number for a hazardous material appear?

options.text: On a bumper sticker on the vehicle.

questions.explanation: The ID number must appear on the packaging and on shipping papers. It must also appear on cargo tanks and bulk packaging.

questions.question: What is the correct way to check tire pressure?

options.text: Push on the tire with your hand.

questions.explanation: Check your tires at the start of each trip and after every stop. Always use a tire pressure gauge to check if tires are properly inflated.

questions.question: If "G" appears in Column 1 of a shipping paper, what else must be listed?

options.text: The technical name of the hazardous material.
The date the product was packed.

questions.correctAnswerText: The technical name of the hazardous material.
questions.explanation: If "G" (meaning "Generic") is in Column 1 of shipping papers, the technical name of the hazardous material must also be listed.

questions.question: If hazardous materials leak while you are driving, what should you do?

options.text: Park the vehicle as soon as possible.
Drive around looking for someone to fix the leak.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park the vehicle as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: If cargo leaks while you are driving, stop immediately. Do not drive farther than necessary, as this spreads the contamination. Park the vehicle, secure the area, and send someone else for help.

questions.question: Where should you load hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: Always load hazardous materials away from heat sources. Heat can make many materials more dangerous.

questions.question: What does a material's hazard class tell you?

options.text: The risks associated with the material.
How much packaging is needed for the shipment.
Where on the trailer items can be placed.
How to load and unload the material.

questions.correctAnswerText: The risks associated with the material.
questions.explanation: There are nine hazard classes. Each class shows the risks associated with that type of material.

questions.question: To get a HazMat endorsement, which agency must check your background?
questions.explanation: To get a new or renewed HazMat endorsement, you must pass a background check from the Transportation Security Administration (TSA).

questions.question: If a package is too small for a hazard label, how should it be labeled?

options.text: Bundle it with other hazardous materials and attach a labeled sheet to the outside.
Attach the label to a tag that is securely fastened to the package.
Mark the item with a large orange dot.
Place the item in a box that displays a warning label.

questions.correctAnswerText: Attach the label to a tag that is securely fastened to the package.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped hazard labels must be placed on hazardous material packages. If the label does not fit, attach it to a tag that is securely fastened to the package.
